submission.reasoning: On workstation5, services.exe (PID 716, C:\Windows\System32\services.exe) started svchost.exe (PID 1884) as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM at 04:19:07Z. The command line was 'svchost.exe -k netsvcs -p -s gpsvc', which is the Group Policy Client service. The binary sits at the standard System32 path, and its file metadata names Microsoft Corporation and original filename svchost.exe. Its only registry activity was two DWORD 0 values written right after start, which fits normal Group Policy processing. Nothing points to injection, masquerading or persistence. This is a normal service start, so the verdict is benign.
